figures.caption: Figure 1: (a) Compilation time vs. enum cardinality (Qwen3-8B, log-log scale). Dotted lines mark documented provider limits (Gemini ∼120, Anthropic ∼200, OpenAI 1,000). The trie is flat at 30–67ms; XGrammar crosses the trie at K≈300 and reaches 2.7s at K=100K. (b) End-to-end vLLM throughput (log scale). The 29× gap at B=256 combines 7× per-step algorithmic advantage with integration-path savings from precomputed masks (Section 5).

Figure 2: The BPE-trie alignment problem. A character-level trie encodes three enum values with shared prefix structure. BPE tokens (colored brackets) span multiple trie edges: medic traverses 5 character nodes from the root. At each node, we precompute the set of valid BPE tokens (right), enabling precomputed mask lookups at decode time.
Table 1: Complexity comparison between FSM and trie automaton. Concrete values use K = 2,000, Lmax = 30, |Σ| = 256, V = 32,000, ℓ = 4.

Prompts identical within each pair; trie is the only difference. Trie guarantees 100% validity. Full results (6 models) in Appendix Table 7.
